units.translation: or the bright one, the one gathered because of brightness, or the one who despises and holds no account because of harshness; or the sharp one compared to the awns
when it reaps. Or reaping, or the one gathered because of brightness, sharp, or of the ears of corn

The grammarians cited at fr. 351 record the comparative form ὑπερτερώτερος [more superior] from Aeschylus: hence Weilius conjectured that at Ag. 428, for τάδ᾽ ἐστὶ καὶ τῶνδ᾽ ὑπερβατώτερα, ὑπερτερώτερα [these things are and more surpassing than those, more superior] should be restored.
But indeed Nemesis is superior to us.
Zeus, indeed, is all things and whatever is superior to these.
You might speak if you have anything superior to these.
He swears by the spear, which he trusts to revere more than the god, and by the eyes, as superior.
these things are and more surpassing than those, more superior
But who would speak of the exceedingly bold thought of a man?
Aristophanes Nub. 1134 called a very intense voice ὑπέρτονον βοάν [a very intense cry].
Let the trumpet sound its very intense voice to the army.
You have spoken a pollution not surpassable.

where strangely is added ὑπὲρ τὸ βέλτιστον [beyond the best], where you might rather expect μέτρον δὲ βέλτιστον [but measure is best], which Weilius conjectured. Moreover, the word ὑπέρφευ [excessively] (in the codex ὑπερφ., wrongly changed to ὑπερφυῶς [excessively]) Hesychius explains by ὑπεράγαν [exceedingly], and Phrynicus touched on it twice in Bekker's Anecdota p. 51, 26 μηδὲν ὑπέρφευ: ἐπὶ (ἀντὶ Blomfield) τοῦ μηδὲν ἄγαν [nothing excessively: for (instead of) nothing too much]. and p. 69, 27 ὑπὲρ τὸ φεῦ: οἷον ὑπερβαλλόντως καὶ ἐκπληκτικῶς · τὸ γὰρ φεῦ ἐπὶ ἐκπλήξεως τίθεται [beyond the alas: as it were surpassingly and astonishingly; for the alas is used for astonishment]. We leave the article in the middle whether it is due to the grammarian or the scribe: for it is not likely that anyone said otherwise than ὑπέρφευ [excessively]. Besides Aeschylus, Euripides used this adverb twice, Phoen. 550 τί τὴν τυραννίδα τιμᾶς ὑπέρφευ [why do you honor tyranny excessively]; and Herc. f. 1321 εἰ σὺ μὲν – φέρεις ὑπέρφευ τὰς τύχας [if you, on the one hand, bear your fortunes excessively], where it is too heavily. As to the accent, it is wrongly perispomenon in the codex of Hesychius. The correct accent is ὑπέρφευ [excessively], as it is written ὑπέρ-eu, not ὑπερεῦ.
It is not right for a mortal to think excessively.
of houses abounding excessively, beyond the best,
beyond the alas: as it were surpassingly and astonishingly; for the alas is used for astonishment
why do you honor tyranny excessively
if you, on the one hand, bear your fortunes excessively
Be at ease, and do not fear excessively.
